controls: Enumerate m1/m2/m4/m8 x unroll=1/2/4/8 with instruction-level live intervals and reject any candidate beyond LMUL*peak_live<=32
Compute LMUL from runtime vlenb (e.g. get_platform_vlen) with an m1 fallback for unknown or vlenb<16 targets
Inspect emitted disassembly for spills/v0 conflicts at m4 before shipping; keep runtime-VL strip mining and tail coverage
Gate behind mayiuse(v) and keep the scalar/reference reorder fallback for non-RVV builds
reasons: Larger LMUL changes the live register-group footprint; underestimating peak live vectors (accumulators, v0, widening EMUL, allocator scratch) can spill at m4/m8
VLEN is a runtime property; a fixed m4 assumption would be wrong on vlenb<16 or different SEW and could emit illegal vtype
m4 occupies 4 consecutive vector registers and requires group alignment; conflict with v0 or the allocator would break other emission paths in the same generator

conditions.description: RVV available at runtime (mayiuse(v)) on the C920v2 target
emit_pure_copy_core path selected: interim_f32_ false (pure f32->f32, no scales/zp/beta/compensation) and unit strides is0==os0==1
node[0].n=16 and VLEN=128 so e32/m4 yields VLMAX=16 covering the whole row
no attrs on this reorder, so the emit_core conversion path is not involved

actions.proposal: In jit_uni_reorder_kernel_f32_t::emit_pure_copy_core (src/cpu/rv64/reorder/jit_uni_reorder_kernel.cpp) select LMUL from runtime VLEN and node[0].n instead of the hardcoded m1: for e32 on VLEN=128, LMUL=m4 yields VLMAX=16 equal to node[0].n, collapsing the four inner iterations per 16-element row into one; enforce LMUL * peak_live_vectors <= 32 (only one live vector v8 plus transients live), validate group alignment, and retain an m1 fallback when the budget or vlenb is unknown. This is an emitter emission change, not a source-level loop rewrite.

correctness_checks: Element-by-element bit-exact compare of reorder output vs reference for f32->f32 unit-stride configs
Tail coverage for node[0] counts 0..16 and non-multiples of VLMAX
benchdnn conv_f32_upstream self-check passes; emitted disassembly shows no vector spill, no vlmul_ext/vlmul_trunc
Dispatch on runtime vlenb, not a fixed VLEN constant

Dynamic instruction count of the reorder kernel per element falls; back-edge and branch counts drop as the inner loop collapses to one iteration per row
If LMUL is over-sized beyond the live-set budget, vector spill/reload (stack vector loads/stores) or a v0/group-alignment conflict appears in the emitted code

success_criteria: Inner loop iterations per 16-element row drop from 4 to 1 on VLEN=128 (one vsetvli/vle/vse per row)

controls: Gate the transformation on is0==os0==1 and itype==otype==4-byte so the fixed step and shared offset are provably valid
Keep a separate tail path for partial-VL iterations where the step is not VLMAX*4
Compute end pointers in 64-bit and assert boundary arithmetic before entering the loop
Run the element-by-element comparison and benchdnn self-check after emission change
reasons: VL is not constant across a row's inner iterations (16,12,8,4), so a fixed addi applies only to full-VL steps; incorrect tail gating would advance pointers too far
end = base + n*stride can wrap if the range exceeds the address space

conditions.description: base + n*4 within the address space without overflow

actions.proposal: In emit_pure_copy_core's vl-loop, replace the per-iteration index scaling (mul reg_tmp0_,reg_vl_,reg_istride_; add reg_addr_,reg_addr_,reg_tmp0_ and the oside pair) with induction-variable pointer increments: precompute src_end/dst_end = base + n*stride once before the loop, advance both pointers by a constant step (addi VLMAX*4 = 16 bytes on VLEN=128 e32/m1) on full-VL iterations, compare pointers against the precomputed ends, and keep a mul/VL-based advance only for the partial tail. When reg_istride_==reg_ostride_ (both 4 here), emit one shared offset instead of two identical muls.

correctness_checks: Zero-length (n==0) must execute zero iterations; single element; exact 16-element row; non-multiple-of-VLMAX tail lengths
Bit-exact copy equality vs reference with no off-by-one at the end pointer
Shared-offset reuse (one advance for both pointers) must be gated on reg_istride_==reg_ostride_ to avoid corrupting addresses in non-unit configs
64-bit end-pointer arithmetic; verify no wrap near the address limit

review_items.description: Re-profile with a V-enabled disassembler/annotate build and confirm the vsetvli vtype word encodes e32/m1 and VLMAX=4 on VLEN=128.
Collect perf record with call-graph over the benchdnn conv_f32_upstream run and compute this function's share of total cycles (e.g. perf report --no-children).
Confirm mayiuse(v) dispatch selects jit_uni_reorder_kernel_f32 on the C920v2 target and that no scalar fallback path contributes to the sampled function.

alternative_explanations.explanation: cpu-clock sampling on the out-of-order C920v2 can cluster retired-instruction IPs at one loop instruction (the mul at 0xfc) when the ROB head stalls on a dependency or memory event, so the mul may not literally consume 89% of cycles. The structural conclusion (VLMAX=4, 16-byte steps, heavy scalar bookkeeping on a loop-carried address chain) is unchanged because it rests on the source-level loop shape and register budget.

The loop could be memory/bandwidth bound rather than control bound. L1 dcache load miss rate is only 1.897% and each iteration moves just 16 bytes, far below the core's bandwidth, so instruction/dependency overhead dominates rather than memory.

findings.conclusion: The f32->f32 reorder kernel jit_uni_reorder_kernel_f32.6 is an already-vectorized copy loop whose LMUL=m1 (SEW=e32) on VLEN=128 delivers only VLMAX=4 elements per vector step, forcing four 9-instruction inner iterations to copy each 16-element row and 16 per call; the loop-carried pointer-advance chain (vsetvli->mul->add->next vle) serializes the tiny 16-byte steps, concentrating 88.98% of function samples on the address-scaling mul at 0xfc.

neighbor_exclusions.reason: The per-iteration vsetvli is semantically required (AVL 16,12,8,4 decreasing) and is not duplicate/redundant vector-state bookkeeping; the root issue is the LMUL choice (m1 below the legal frontier), which register-group utilization owns.

findings.reasoning: The sampled kernel is jit_uni_reorder_kernel_f32_t::emit_pure_copy_core (f32->f32 unit-stride copy). Source uses vsetvli(reg_vl_, reg_rem_, SEW::e32, LMUL::m1) so VLMAX=4 on VLEN=128 (vlenb=16, C920v2). The 16-element node[0] therefore needs 4 inner iterations per row and 4 rows (node[1].n=4) give 16 vector steps per call, each advancing only 16 bytes. 88.98% of the 118 function samples land on the loop-carried pointer-offset mul at 0xfc; the loop body is 6 scalar bookkeeping instructions (2 mul, 2 add, sub, j) around 2 vector instructions. LMUL=m1 is far below the legal frontier: only one vector register is live (v8) plus transients, so LMUL*peak_live <= 32 holds for m4 (VLMAX=16 = node[0].n), collapsing the inner loop to one iteration per row.

alternative_explanations.explanation: VL is not constant across the four inner iterations of a row (16,12,8,4), so a naive fixed addi advance must be gated to full-VL steps; part of the mul-based advance remains for the tail iteration, limiting but not eliminating the strength-reduction gain.

The two muls are not needed because src and dst strides differ: reg_istride_ and reg_ostride_ are both 4 bytes (a4==a5==4) for this unit-stride configuration, so the two mul+add pairs compute identical values.

findings.conclusion: The pointer advance inside the hot copy loop is expressed as per-iteration index scaling (two identical mul t3*4 plus two adds) instead of induction-variable pointer increments with a precomputed end-pointer comparison; in the steady state VL is constant (VLMAX=4, 16 bytes), so this is 4 instructions of redundant loop-control work per 16-byte vector step.

neighbor_exclusions.reason: Peephole single-instruction identities route to algebraic simplification; this conclusion claims loop-level induction-variable strength reduction (per-iteration mul+add index scaling to pointer increments plus precomputed end pointer), which the loop-level row owns.

findings.reasoning: Disassembly shows the pointer advance recomputed every iteration as mul t0,t3,a4; add t4,t4,t0; mul t0,t3,a5; add t5,t5,t0 (a4==a5==4): index scaling of VL*4 twice per 16-byte step. Source emit_pure_copy_core emits the same mul(reg_tmp0_,reg_vl_,reg_istride_); add; mul; add; sub; j sequence. With VL at VLMAX=4 in steady state the advance is a constant 16 bytes, so two induction variables incrementing by addi 16 plus an end-pointer comparison replace 4-6 scalar instructions per iteration; the same leverage also removes the duplicate same-operand mul.

alternative_explanations.explanation: The fixed m1 loop shape with duplicate mul pairs may be a deliberate emitter simplicity/code-size trade-off rather than an oversight; the profile shows it dominates a memory-movement kernel, so it remains actionable.

Only the pure-copy fast path (interim_f32_ false, unit strides) uses emit_pure_copy_core; configs with scales/zp/beta use emit_core and may not exhibit the same shape. The conclusion is scoped to the actually-sampled pure-copy path.

findings.conclusion: The JIT emitter (jit_uni_reorder_kernel_f32_t::emit_pure_copy_core) always emits the fixed LMUL=m1 loop shape with duplicate same-operand mul pairs (a4==a5==4) and sub/j bookkeeping regardless of the actual geometry (node[0]=16, VLEN=128), so the code-generation contract failed to specialize the hot copy loop.

neighbor_exclusions.reason: The correct JIT kernel is selected and samples are dominated by its emitted loop body; the issue is emission quality (fixed m1 shape, duplicate mul), not a wrong fallback or dispatch guard.
The JIT row owns the emitter contract that always emits the m1 duplicate-mul shape; the loop-level row owns induction-variable shape inside a given emitted loop.

findings.reasoning: The hotspot lies in code emitted by oneDNN's RISC-V JIT reorder emitter. emit_pure_copy_core unconditionally emits the m1 loop with two identical muls (a4==a5==4), a sub counter and a j back-edge regardless of VLEN or node[0].n: the emitter/representation contract never specialized the loop to the small unit-stride copy geometry, so every emitted instruction lands directly on the workload's execution path.

asm.reason: Hotspot resides entirely in JIT-generated reorder kernel (jitted-11579-6.so, jit_uni_reorder_kernel_f32.6); no handwritten .S kernel is implicated or dominating the measured hotspot.

codegen.reason: JIT-generated loop shows codegen artifacts: duplicate mul (t0,t3,a4 and t0,t3,a5) computing identical 4-byte offsets plus scalar mul/add pointer bookkeeping inside the vector loop; 88.98% of samples land on the first mul at 0xfc.

crypto.reason: No cryptographic arithmetic, cipher modes, hashes, checksums, or binary-field work appears in the reorder kernel disassembly.

offload.reason: No packed-SIMD, matrix-engine, or parallel GEMM offload evidence; kernel is unit-stride RVV load/store with scalar pointer updates.
